# WO-2026-08-13-16 — the third field: `display_name`

**This is Warwick's own product design, in his words:**

> *"Can you create a third linked field called display name? Asda listing is the official one, Alias is what
> mum writes on her lists but neither should be editable but alias shouldn't necessarily be displayed.
> Display name would be a name I can enter/amend/edit on a page on my cockpit. I think on mums dashboard we
> should have the display name large and then the official asda name quite small running in one line at the
> bottom of the tile, so its easy for me to see what it actually is."*

**⛔ WHY THIS DESIGN IS BETTER THAN THE ONE IT REPLACES, and it governs your build.** Larry's earlier plan
was to edit `aka`. **`aka` is the MATCHER'S input** — `resolveByCatalogue.js:37` reads it to decide which
product a written line means. Editing it to improve what Mum *reads* would silently change what *matches*:
renaming the BOB milk to "milk" would have made every written "milk" ambiguous against the Cravendale.
**Warwick's separation makes that impossible. `display_name` MUST NEVER be read by the matcher.**

**THE THREE FIELDS, and their boundaries:**

| field | what it is | editable? | who reads it |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | the official ASDA listing. **The truth about what the product is** | **NO** | the matcher, and Mum's tile as a small sub-line |
| `aka` | what Mum writes on her lists. **A MATCHING TERM** | **NO** | the matcher **only** |
| **`display_name`** | **NEW.** What Mum reads | **YES — Warwick, from his Cockpit** | Mum's tile **only** |

## Acceptance criteria

**AC1 — migration `021_regulars_display_name.sql`, additive and idempotent.**
`ALTER TABLE asdair.regulars ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS display_name text` — **nullable, no default, no
backfill in the migration.** Follow `020_shop_line_provenance_and_human_state.sql`'s conventions exactly.
**⚠️ 020's own recorded hazard is your warning: it carried a backfill that would OVERWRITE a human's value
on re-run. Yours must be re-runnable with a human-entered value present and change nothing.** Prove that by
executing it twice with a value set.

**AC2 — grants, and they are the point of the boundary.**
`asdair_rw` needs `UPDATE (display_name)` on `asdair.regulars` — **column-scoped if the estate's existing
grants allow it.** State by execution what `asdair_rw` can and cannot update after your migration. **`name`
and `aka` must NOT become writable through anything you add.**

**AC3 — `display_name` is read out and reaches the workspace payload.**
`readWorkspace.js` already carries `name`, `aka` and the display fields Mum's page consumes. Add
`display_name` alongside — **do not replace anything.** Mum's page needs `display_name` AND `name` together,
because Warwick's tile shows both.

**AC4 — the write route. `POST /asdair/display-name`, and it writes ONE column.**
```
request  { "id": <regulars.id>, "display_name": "<text>"|null }
200      { "ok": true, "id": <n>, "display_name": "<text>"|null }
4xx/5xx  { "ok": false, "error": "<machine_code>", "message": "<ONE plain sentence>" }
```
- **`null` or empty clears it** — Warwick must be able to undo a bad name, not just overwrite it.
- **Trim, but do NOT otherwise normalise.** His words are his.
- **A sane length cap** (propose one; 60 chars is a suggestion, not a ruling) with a JSON error, not a truncation.
- **⛔ THE ROUTE MUST BE STRUCTURALLY INCAPABLE OF WRITING `name` OR `aka`.** Not "does not" — *cannot*.
  Build it as a single-column UPDATE with the column name as a literal, never from input. **Prove it by
  execution: an attempt carrying `name` or `aka` in the body must leave both untouched.**
- Proxy it through `services/cockpit/server.mjs` as `/api/asdair/display-name`, same JSON-error discipline
  as the list route.

**AC5 — the matcher NEVER sees `display_name`, and this is proven not asserted.**
`resolveByCatalogue.js` is **outside your surface and must not change.** Prove by execution that setting a
`display_name` which would match a *different* product — set the Cravendale's `display_name` to
`"BOB milk"` — **changes nothing about resolution.** That is the whole safety property of Warwick's design
and it deserves a real test, not a comment.

**AC6 — `display_name` never reaches the matcher's catalogue payload.**
Check `loadCatalogue.js` / `compactRegular` (outside your surface — **report, do not edit**): if adding the
column to a SELECT would carry it into the model prompt, say so loudly. **A display name in the interpreter's
prompt is a new invention surface.**
